_provenance.note: WS-5.2 (2026-08-30): mechanism (CKM_HKDF_DERIVE) already implemented; this closes real Tier-1 KAT coverage. Used the Sp800-56Cr1 revision (not Cr2) because every Cr2 sample test group uses a hybrid PQC+classical shared secret construction with no local spec text to correctly implement — Cr1 has 200 non-hybrid groups covering all fixedInfoPattern/hash combinations this engine needs. fixedInfo (SP800-56C OtherInfo, "concatenation" encoding) is built by the test harness per the official ACVP KDA-HKDF spec (draft-hammett-acvp-kas-kdf-hkdf, usnistgov/ACVP repo, §FixedInfoPatternConstruction): uPartyId||ephemeralData||vPartyId||ephemeralData||BE32(l_bits), verified against this doc’s own worked example before use. 1 AFT + 1 VAL case per hmacAlg (10 of the 11 possible — SHA-1 has zero groups in this sample set, all others do), plus 1 deliberate VAL testPassed=false case (SHA2-256) to confirm mismatches are genuinely detected, not just that matches pass. This also required fixing a real, separate bug found along the way: SoftHSM_keygen.cpp ckmToDigestName() was missing CKM_SHA224/CKM_SHA3_224/CKM_SHA512_224/CKM_SHA512_256, so HKDF with those four PRF hashes was unusable regardless of test coverage. NOTE (2026-08-30, post-hoc): the FIRST extraction of this file picked VAL tests[0] blind, without checking the testPassed field — ACVP KDA VAL groups mix testPassed=true/false cases like any other VAL-type test, and 4 of the 10 picked cases (SHA2-256/384/512/512-256) happened to be testPassed=false. Re-extracted to select the first testPassed=true case per group instead, and added one explicit testPassed=false case so the negative path has real, intentional coverage rather than being an accident of extraction order.
